title: the Ninefold Court Rising Again
premise: Oscar Underhill, the last swordspeaker, has hidden her gift for twelve years in the magic-hating city of Vell, selling charms that work by luck rather than spell. When the crown's witchfinders begin burning anyone with the gift, she is dragged into the resistance by a dying oath-sworn knight who names her heir to the Ninefold Court—a council of nine magic-bearers destroyed by the king. Oscar discovers the king died years ago and the thing wearing his crown is a hollowed revenant feeding on the city's bound magic. To save Vell, she must gather the scattered remnants of the nine courts, unbind the king's corpse from the crown, and accept that her own oath—the one that silenced her—must be broken. In the end she speaks her true name aloud, shatters the crown, and chooses to rebuild the Court not as rulers but as guardians, finally belonging somewhere she once fled.
about_author: Paloma Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist from Marseille who writes fantasy about oaths, cities, and the people who survive both. Her work is known for quiet magic, morally crowded courts, and endings that cost something.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the market of Vell, Oscar sells a luck-charm to a frightened child while concealing the swordspeech humming under her skin. A witchfinder's procession passes, and an old woman is dragged away. Oscar does nothing. Emotional beat: the shame of survival, and the first crack in her conviction that hiding is the same as being safe.

chapters.title: The Knight at the Door
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A dying knight, Ser Aldric Vane, collapses in her shop with the sigil of the Ninefold Court burned into his hand. He names her heir before witchfinders arrive, forcing her to use her gift publicly to escape. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant awakening—her invisibility is over whether she likes it or not.

chapters.title: What the Crown Forbids
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Hiding in the undercity, Oscar learns the history she was raised on: the Ninefold Court weren't tyrants but the kingdom's balance, destroyed when the king declared magic treason. She meets Nessa, a thief with a spark of gift, and realizes the hunt is a harvest. Emotional beat: grief for a history stolen from her.

chapters.title: Nine Names, Nine Graves
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following Aldric's notes, Oscar visits the first of nine hidden vaults and finds a court-token that responds to her blood. Each token carries a memory of its dead bearer. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead, and the growing weight of an inheritance she never asked for.

chapters.title: The Witchfinder's Mercy
chapters.summary: Witchfinder Captain Ilsa Reyne's POV. Reyne burns a gifted family but secretly spares a child, revealing her own buried gift and her bargain with the crown: serve, or be served. Emotional beat: the corruption of power—Reyne believes she is the reasonable one, and almost is.

chapters.title: A Market of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar seeks the oath-breaker Brann, once the Court's smith, who refuses to help because the Court's last act doomed his daughter. Oscar must speak a fragment of her swordspeech to prove herself, and the city hears it. Emotional beat: the cost of being seen; power used honestly for the first time in twelve years.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Throne Room
chapters.summary: Reyne's POV. Summoned before the king, Reyne realizes the monarch hasn't aged in a decade and that his shadow moves wrong. The crown speaks to her, offering to legitimize her gift if she delivers the last swordspeaker. Emotional beat: seduction of power; Reyne accepts, telling herself she'll control it.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The second and third vaults yield tokens, but the crown's soldiers torch the coastal town where the fourth was hidden. Oscar pulls survivors from the fire with Nessa and Brann, and a ragged band forms around her without her consent. Emotional beat: unwanted leadership; belonging arriving before she's ready for it.

chapters.title: The Oath That Silenced Her
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In a memory-token, Oscar relives the night her mother bound her voice with the Last Oath—a vow of silence taken to hide her from the purge. She learns the oath is also a leash the crown can pull. Emotional beat: fury and tenderness toward the mother who muzzled her to save her.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Undercity
chapters.summary: Reyne's POV. Reyne tracks Oscar through Vell's tunnels, and the two women finally speak—enemy to enemy, gift to gift. Reyne offers Oscar the crown's bargain: kneel and live. Oscar refuses, and Reyne lets her go, one heartbeat too long. Emotional beat: recognition between mirrors; the reader sees Reyne's corruption is a choice renewed daily.

chapters.title: The Sixth Seat Is Empty
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The sixth token belongs to the Court's traitor—the one who opened the gates for the king. Oscar learns the purge began with a betrayal by magic itself, and that the crown's revenant was born from that broken trust. Emotional beat: disillusionment; her cause is not clean, and neither was the Court.

chapters.title: What Nessa Carries
chapters.summary: Nessa's POV. Nessa's small gift flares into something dangerous when soldiers corner the group; she kills for the first time and nearly loses herself to the power. Oscar talks her back using swordspeech as a lifeline. Emotional beat: power as addiction; Oscar sees her own possible future in the girl.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Reyne's POV. The crown begins wearing Reyne as much as she wears it, feeding on her suppressed gift. She discovers records proving the king has been dead twelve years—the same twelve years Oscar has been hiding. Emotional beat: horror and the first honest doubt; Reyne starts planning her own defection.

chapters.title: The Gathering of the Nine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the ruined Court hall beneath the palace, Oscar sets the recovered tokens on their thrones and speaks the opening of the Ninefold rite. The dead answer—not as ghosts, but as voices in the stones, each demanding a price. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the past is not done with the living.

chapters.title: A Price for Every Voice
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Court's voices each demand a sacrifice: Brann must forgive the traitor, Nessa must surrender her gift's growth, Oscar must give up the name she has hidden behind. She stalls, and the rite begins to fail. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—power demands identity, and identity cannot be kept safe.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Hall
chapters.summary: Reyne's POV and Oscar's. Reyne leads the witchfinders to the hall—but at the threshold she turns on her own soldiers, buying the group time and taking a mortal wound. Dying, she gives Oscar the crown's true weakness: the revenant is bound by the king's original oath, still unspoken. Emotional beat: redemption purchased too late, but purchased.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With Vell's bells tolling the hunt's endgame, Oscar, Nessa, and Brann fight through the palace's upper reaches as the crown drains the city's magic to complete its reign. Brann falls covering their retreat. Emotional beat: rising dread; every ally is a cost, and the climb feels like the whole kingdom's weight.

chapters.title: The King Who Was Not
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the throne room, Oscar faces the revenant and the corpse it wears. It offers her the eighth seat and the ninth—rule beside it, restore the Court as tyrants, make magic safe forever by making it lawless. Emotional beat: the darkest temptation; the corruption of power offered in the shape of everything she's lost.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Last Oath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. To unbind the king, Oscar must break her mother's oath and speak her true name—Oscarina Underhill, swordspeaker, daughter of the Court's last voice. The words tear the binding from the dead king's throat, and the revenant loses its anchor. Emotional beat: identity as weapon and liberation; the silence of twelve years ending in one sentence.

chapters.title: Crownfall
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The freed king's spirit, given one breath, completes the rite with Oscar and the nine voices, shattering the crown. Magic floods back into Vell—terrifying, unregulated, alive. Oscar stands in the wreckage holding the crown's shards, the most powerful and most feared person in the city. Emotional beat: triumph hollowed by cost; power won is power to be answered for.

chapters.title: The Ninth Seat
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weeks later, Vell argues over what comes next. Oscar refuses a throne and instead convenes a new Ninefold Court of the living—gifted and ungifted, including Nessa—sworn to guard rather than govern. She takes the ninth seat herself, openly, under her true name. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; power bound by accountability.

chapters.title: Swordspeech, Sung Plainly
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing. In the rebuilt market, Oscar sells charms that actually work, teaches a gifted child her first word of power, and visits the graves of Brann, Reyne, and her mother. The last line of her oath is rewritten: not silence, but service. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—identity no longer hidden, power no longer feared, home finally real.
